key_insight: Multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence can separate interfacial from bulk degradation in perovskite solar cells, revealing that PEABF4 improves the ETL/perovskite interface initially but accelerates depth-spreading recombination losses under heat.
engineering_relevance: This provides a nondestructive diagnostic for tracking where stability improvements fail during aging, helping engineers optimize interface treatments and reliability strategies in perovskite devices.
method: Used wavelength-dependent PL mapping to probe different excitation depths nondestructively.
Compared PEABF4-treated perovskite stacks before and after thermal aging.
Interpreted PL decay trends with diffusion-recombination simulations to distinguish surface recombination velocity from bulk lifetime changes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that PEABF4 reduces interfacial recombination losses initially, but after thermal stress the PL signatures broaden from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber, consistent with faster degradation.
watch_item: The approach infers depth-dependent degradation from modeling and PL response, so calibration against complementary structural or electrical measurements may still be needed for definitive mechanism assignment.
paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
